# IndustReal toy-car assembly — state-transition analysis playbook

You are analyzing ONE silent egocentric (head-mounted camera) video of a person
assembling / reworking a construction-toy car. Videos are 1280x720 @ 10 fps.
Your job: produce the chronological list of **stable assembly-state checkpoints**.

## The 11 tracked components (fixed index order)
| idx | component | real-world appearance in these videos |
|--:|--|--|
| 0 | base | WHITE thick 3-D **block** (has depth, not a flat bar) with 4 round through-holes. Central spine piece; the starting piece in full-build videos. |
| 1 | front chassis | WHITE **flat bar, 5 holes** (medium length). Attaches to one end of the base. |
| 2 | front chassis pin | GRAY metal pin (short) with a pronged/flat head; passes through base+front chassis. Usually capped with a MAGENTA nut. Normally installed together with the front chassis. |
| 3 | rear chassis | WHITE **flat bar, 6 holes** (the LONGEST bar). The correct rear spine piece. |
| 4 | short rear chassis | WHITE **flat bar, 4 holes** (the SHORTEST bar). NOT part of the correct car — should stay ABSENT (0). Only appears if the person makes a mistake / test-fits it. |
| 5 | front-rear chassis pin | GRAY pin joining rear chassis to base at the FRONT of that joint; capped with MAGENTA nut. |
| 6 | rear-rear chassis pin | GRAY pin joining rear chassis at the REAR of that joint; capped with MAGENTA nut. |
| 7 | front bracket | WHITE **U / L-shaped angular bracket** (distinct bent shape, not a flat bar). Mounts on TOP at the front; carries the front axle. |
| 8 | front bracket screw | LONG GRAY screw standing tall through the front bracket, capped with a MAGENTA nut. (In the reference render it is the tall red screw sticking straight up.) |
| 9 | front wheel assembly | An axle carrying TWO black tires (magenta hubs), mounted at the FRONT (through/under the front bracket). |
| 10 | rear wheel assembly | An axle carrying TWO black tires (magenta hubs), mounted at the REAR (through the rear chassis). |

Other loose things on the table (piles of magenta rings = spare nuts, spare gray
pins/screws, spare white bars, stacked spare tires) are INVENTORY, not installed.
Only count a component when it is mechanically attached to the growing assembly.

## State value encoding
For each component at each checkpoint: `1` = correctly installed, `-1` = installed
but clearly wrong (wrong hole/orientation/part, not seated), `0` = absent.
Default to `1` when a part is attached and looks normal; only use `-1` when the error
is clearly visible (e.g. the short-rear-chassis used in place of the rear chassis, a
bar in the wrong holes, a pin/bar visibly not seated that is later corrected).

## Reference "correct" states (binary, idx0..idx10 left→right, 1=present&correct)
state1  10000000000  base only
state2  10010010000  base+rear chassis+rear-rear pin
state3  10010100000  base+rear chassis+front-rear pin
state4  10010110000  base+rear chassis+both rear pins
state5  11100000000  base+front chassis+front chassis pin
state6  11110010000  +rear chassis+rear-rear pin
state7  11110100000  +rear chassis+front-rear pin
state8  11110110000  base+FC+FCpin+rear chassis+both rear pins
state9  11110111100  +front bracket+front bracket screw
state10 11110111110  +front wheel assembly
state11 11110110001  ...+rear wheel assembly (no bracket yet)
state12 11110111101  +rear wheel assembly
state13 11110111111  COMPLETE car (all 11 of the tracked-correct set = 1; note idx4 short-rear stays 0)
(states 14-22 are the same complete set with various wheel/pin subsets removed —
used to describe dis-assembly. idx4 is 0 in every reference state.)

Typical correct build order: install base → front chassis (+its pin) → rear chassis
(+front-rear pin, +rear-rear pin) → front bracket (+its screw) → wheels. Rework videos
start from a near-complete car, remove some parts, then reinstall them.

## What is a checkpoint (READ CAREFULLY)
A checkpoint is anchored to the **earliest frame where one or more component states
change**, i.e. the state-transition frame — NOT the end of the hand action.
- correct-install: first frame the component is fully & correctly attached (incl. its
  required pin/screw/nut/tightening).
- incorrect-install: first frame the component is present but in a wrong state.
- removal: first frame a previously-installed component is no longer mechanically
  attached (even if the hand still holds it or sets it down later).
- If a hand occludes the exact instant, use the earliest frame where the NEW state can
  be confirmed. Do NOT wait for hands to leave, the part to be set on the desk, the
  person to inspect, or the next action to start.
- A single transition can change several components at once (e.g. bar+its pin, or a
  2-wheel axle) → ONE checkpoint listing the full state after.
- The component states already present at 00:00 are INITIAL CONDITIONS, not a
  checkpoint. Report them separately as `initial_state`.
- Ignore pure hand motions, picking up loose parts, or touching/aligning before the
  state actually changes.
- Timestamps must be on the ABSOLUTE video timeline (seconds from that video's 0.0),
  accurate within ~2 s of the transition frame.

## Method (use ffmpeg; be efficient but thorough)
Helper: `bash /workspace/work/montage.sh VIDEO START DUR INTERVAL COLS ROWS TW TH OUT`
burns the ABSOLUTE timestamp into each tile. Example dense montage:
`bash /workspace/work/montage.sh /workspace/materials/X.mp4 40 40 2 5 4 480 270 /workspace/work/frames/X_40.png`
Then `Read` the PNG.
1. Coarse pass (already have ~every-5-6 s overview available, or make your own) to
   locate WHERE the assembly visibly changes.

11	| 1 | front chassis | WHITE **flat bar, 5 holes** (medium length). Attaches to one end of the base. |
12	| 2 | front chassis pin | GRAY metal pin (short) with a pronged/flat head; passes through base+front chassis. Usually capped with a MAGENTA nut. Normally installed together with the front chassis. |
13	| 3 | rear chassis | WHITE **flat bar, 6 holes** (the LONGEST bar). The correct rear spine piece. |
14	| 4 | short rear chassis | WHITE **flat bar, 4 holes** (the SHORTEST bar). NOT part of the correct car — should stay ABSENT (0). Only appears if the person makes a mistake / test-fits it. |
15	| 5 | front-rear chassis pin | GRAY pin joining rear chassis to base at the FRONT of that joint; capped with MAGENTA nut. |
16	| 6 | rear-rear chassis pin | GRAY pin joining rear chassis at the REAR of that joint; capped with MAGENTA nut. |
17	| 7 | front bracket | WHITE **U / L-shaped angular bracket** (distinct bent shape, not a flat bar). Mounts on TOP at the front; carries the front axle. |
18	| 8 | front bracket screw | LONG GRAY screw standing tall through the front bracket, capped with a MAGENTA nut. (In the reference render it is the tall red screw sticking straight up.) |
19	| 9 | front wheel assembly | An axle carrying TWO black tires (magenta hubs), mounted at the FRONT (through/under the front bracket). |
20	| 10 | rear wheel assembly | An axle carrying TWO black tires (magenta hubs), mounted at the REAR (through the rear chassis). |
21	
22	Other loose things on the table (piles of magenta rings = spare nuts, spare gray
23	pins/screws, spare white bars, stacked spare tires) are INVENTORY, not installed.
24	Only count a component when it is mechanically attached to the growing assembly.
25

27	For each component at each checkpoint: `1` = correctly installed, `-1` = installed
28	but clearly wrong (wrong hole/orientation/part, not seated), `0` = absent.

31	bar in the wrong holes, a pin/bar visibly not seated that is later corrected).

36	state3  10010100000  base+rear chassis+front-rear pin

52	start from a near-complete car, remove some parts, then reinstall them.

56	change**, i.e. the state-transition frame — NOT the end of the hand action.

58	  required pin/screw/nut/tightening).

68	  checkpoint. Report them separately as `initial_state`.
69	- Ignore pure hand motions, picking up loose parts, or touching/aligning before the
70	  state actually changes.

72	  accurate within ~2 s of the transition frame.

56	change**, i.e. the state-transition frame — NOT the end of the hand action.

58	  required pin/screw/nut/tightening).
59	- incorrect-install: first frame the component is present but in a wrong state.
60	- removal: first frame a previously-installed component is no longer mechanically
61	  attached (even if the hand still holds it or sets it down later).

63	  be confirmed. Do NOT wait for hands to leave, the part to be set on the desk, the
64	  person to inspect, or the next action to start.

66	  2-wheel axle) → ONE checkpoint listing the full state after.

68	  checkpoint. Report them separately as `initial_state`.
69	- Ignore pure hand motions, picking up loose parts, or touching/aligning before the
70	  state actually changes.

72	  accurate within ~2 s of the transition frame.

76	burns the ABSOLUTE timestamp into each tile. Example dense montage:

80	   locate WHERE the assembly visibly changes.

82	3. Confirm the exact transition second with full-res single frames:
83	   `ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -ss T -i VIDEO -frames:v 1 -y out.png` (step T
84	   by 0.1-0.5 s across the transition). Zoom by adding `-vf crop=W:H:X:Y,scale=...`.
85	4. Nail the earliest frame the new stable state is confirmable; record that time.
86	Prefer FEWER, well-evidenced checkpoints over speculation. Note uncertainty explicitly.
87	Pins/screws are small — infer them from the magenta nut being seated and from the
88	build logic (a bar is attached BY its pin) when direct view is occluded, but say so.
89	
90	## Output
91	Write `/workspace/work/ledger_X.json` (X = your video letter) EXACTLY as:
92	```
93	{
94	  "video": "X",
95	  "initial_state": [11 ints],
96	  "initial_notes": "what is already assembled at t=0 and why",
97	  "checkpoints": [
98	    {"time_s": 34.2,
99	     "state_after": [11 ints],
100	     "changed": ["front chassis absent->correct", "front chassis pin absent->correct"],
101	     "evidence": "brief: what frame/time proves it, confidence"},
102	    ...
103	  ]
104	}
105	```
106	Rules for your output:
107	- `state_after` is the COMPLETE 11-vector after that checkpoint's changes.
108	- Consecutive `state_after` vectors (starting from `initial_state`) must differ only by
109	  the components you list in `changed`. Keep them consistent.
110	- Sort checkpoints by time. Do not include a t=0 "checkpoint" for pre-existing parts.
111	- Also return a concise text summary of the timeline when you finish.
